_comment: Site configuration for mqtt-publish.py. Every key is optional.
inverter_name  names this SP PRO in its topics: solar-bridge/selectronic/<name>/...
so a second inverter can be added without colliding.
entity_prefix  prefixes object_id/unique_id. Home Assistant keys entities on unique_id,
so changing it orphans their history. Separate from inverter_name on
purpose: that only names topics. A second inverter needs its own prefix.
buckets        minimum seconds between publishes of each state topic. 0 means every
poll. A topic republishes when any field on it changes, so this is what
gives each reading its effective rate.
exclude        globs matched against object_id. An excluded entity is never announced,
so it costs nothing downstream: no discovery config, no state, no
recorder rows. The defaults below are hardware this unit does not have,
each confirmed two ways -- the whole group of related readings sits at
zero and has never moved, and the inverter's own configuration says the
hardware is absent. Delete a line to bring that group back.
quantize       per-entity rounding as {object_id_glob: decimal_places}. Empty means
raw readings go out untouched, which is the default.

_exclude_rationale.bms_*, bmsmodules_*: 42 entities. TechBmsModel reads None and both BMS blocks are entirely zero; no BMS is wired to this unit.
_exclude_rationale.mppt_*, mppttarget_*: 2 entities. An SPMC482 has no solar MPPT; the 176-word MPPT block reads zero throughout.
_exclude_rationale.shunt1_*, shunt2_*: 34 entities. Shunt1Name and Shunt2Name are both None in the inverter's configuration, so no DC shunts are fitted.
_exclude_rationale.*_kaco3/4/5: 33 entities. KacoModel3/4/5 read None -- only two AC-coupled inverters are present (both Primo GEN24 10.0).
_exclude_rationale.networkpower_*: 1 entity. No network power meter: the register SP LINK tests for one reads zero.
_exclude_rationale.*_energy_today_kaco*, *_ac_volts_kaco*,: 14 entities. The SP PRO only polls AC power from a managed AC-coupled inverter over its Modbus RTU link, so only AcPower and AcPowerPeak are populated for any slot. The volts, current, DC and temperature fields exist for KACO-brand inverters, which report more over Selectronic's own protocol; against a Fronius they read zero for every slot including the two that are in use.
_exclude_rationale.*_ac_power_kaco*: 2 entities. Duplicates the live per-inverter AC power, but sourced from the 15-minute block sweep, so it lags and visibly disagrees with the live sensor -- 218 W against 47 W when measured. The peak tracker (*_ac_power_peak_kaco*) is kept: it is not a duplicate.
_exclude_rationale.sp_pro_export_power_limit: Off-grid, so there is nothing to export to. Constant 0 over 26 h of history.
_exclude_rationale.sp_pro_today_float_hours: Redundant rather than empty: it tracked Inverter Run Hours exactly (14.98 vs 14.97, identical value sets), because the system sits on float continuously. Worth knowing that if the two ever diverge, that divergence is real information about the battery not reaching float -- re-enable this if cycling behaviour becomes interesting.
_exclude_rationale.sp_pro_ac_coupled_percent: Constant 0 across 26 h, including the morning charge window when the array is least constrained, so the register appears not to be populated on this firmware. It is the field that would most directly show curtailment commanding, so re-enable it if the system ever runs genuinely unconstrained.
_exclude_rationale.*_ac_export*: 14 entities. Off-grid: no export path exists. All constant 0.
_exclude_rationale.*_today_ac_energy_kaco*: 2 entities. Today-block per-inverter AC-coupled energy, words 24/25, which read 0 even for the two slots that are in use.
_exclude_rationale.*_float_hrs*: 10 entities. Off-grid with a full battery the system sits on float continuously, so these measure elapsed time rather than anything about the battery: the 7-day accumulator reads exactly 168.00 h, its average exactly 24.00 h/day, and today's float hours matched today's inverter run hours to the digit. Run hours are kept, and at the lifetime level the two do differ (195.4 h run against 176.78 h float), so time-not-in-float is still recoverable as the difference if that ever becomes interesting.
_exclude_rationale.<block twins of curated sensors>: 29 entities. Every curated sensor reads a register the block sweep also reads, so each had a raw twin under a different grouping -- battery_soc alongside now_batt_soc_percent, and so on. Matched by register rather than by value, since zeros collide. The curated one is kept: it has the better name, the right device class, and sits on a topic matching how fast the reading actually moves.
_exclude_rationale.sp_pro_inverter_run_hours_today, sp_pro_: Superseded by a single sp_pro_inverter_hours promoted from Technical.InverterRunHrsTotalAcc. One lifetime counter per inverter is enough to show it has not been down; a daily figure resets and would hide a gap.
